resources.string: The tunnel is off. Nothing in your waves is reachable from this device.
Waiting for approval in the browser…
This device is in no wave yet. Enter the address of your control server to join one; the tunnel starts by itself.
In the next wave you join, this device is called %1$s. A wave it is already in keeps the name it got there.
After a restart the tunnel comes back by itself. Android runs one VPN at a time: switch this off if you also use another one and want to choose each time.
no control connection; peers will stop being updated
Paused. This device stays in the wave and can switch it back on without a new approval.
Add another wave at this server
Relay not connected: devices only reachable through it are cut off until it is back.
This server offers no relay. Devices the phone cannot reach directly, such as a connector in a cluster, stay unreachable.
This device was removed from the wave. Log in again to come back; it needs a new approval.
The control server sent a network map that does not carry its signature. Nothing in it was used; the wave keeps the last good one.
This wave did not come up: %1$s
Android runs one VPN at a time. Connecting wave-mesh disconnects the other one, for example Tailscale.
This device leaves the wave and forgets its keys. Joining again needs a new approval.
This phone joins a wave at %1$s once you approve it in the browser.
This phone is already in a wave at %1$s. It can join another one there; you approve it in the browser.
No wave-mesh control server answers at %1$s; its certificate belongs to another service. Enter the address of your control server, not the domain of your wave.
The address %1$s does not exist. Check how your control server\'s address is spelled.
No server answers at %1$s. Check the address and this device\'s connection.
%1$s is not a wave-mesh control server.
The tunnel stopped before the login finished.
The tunnel did not start. The log says more.
Android did not allow the VPN.
the wave core did not start
The tunnel is not running. Connect first.
No connection to the control server: devices still reach each other, but changes do not arrive.
Names in this wave resolve through the tunnel
No resolver for this wave: names will not resolve, addresses still work.
Relay connected: devices behind NAT stay reachable
The relay is not connected: devices only reachable through it are cut off for now.
This server offers no relay: devices the phone cannot reach directly, such as a connector in a cluster, stay unreachable.
Each service gets a real connection through the tunnel, the way a browser would open it.
%1$s: resting, wakes with the first packet
%1$s: online at the server, but never reached from here. Is it running, and does the server offer a relay?
%1$s: reached, but nothing listens on that port
%1$s: no answer. The device that serves it may be down or unreachable.
The log stays on this device until you share it.
wave-mesh sets up a VPN on this device that connects it with the other devices in your wave.
Traffic between your devices runs encrypted with WireGuard, directly from device to device. Where no direct path is possible, it runs encrypted through a relay of your wave.

To join a wave, the app sends the control server you enter this device\'s name, its public keys and the network addresses it can be reached at. Neither the control server nor the relay can read your traffic.
The app sends no data to Moellenbeck Digital. It contains no analytics and no advertising, and no data is sold or passed on.
In the next step Android asks whether wave-mesh may set up a VPN connection.
